findings.claim: The speech API supports Spanish text, but the built-in voices are documented as optimized for English and no Colombian locale-specific voice was documented.
The API is synchronous with chunked streaming and supports MP3, Opus, AAC, FLAC, WAV, and raw 24 kHz 16-bit mono PCM.
The current GPT-4o mini TTS page documents a 2000-token input limit, text and audio-token pricing, and a dated snapshot, while the current model catalog signals deprecation risk.
TTS-1 and TTS-1 HD retain public per-character prices, but are older model families than the guide's recommended GPT-4o mini TTS path.
The reviewed speech API documentation does not document a durable remote job identity, provider-side idempotency key, cancellation, or word-level timing output.
API input and output are not used for training by default; the speech endpoint is documented with 30-day abuse-monitoring retention and Zero Data Retention eligibility.
The TTS guide requires disclosure that the voice is AI generated.
Commercial API use remains subject to the current service agreement and service terms, including output-related limitations and indemnity exclusions that require legal review.
A public status history exists, but standard-tier latency is not generally guaranteed; enterprise service tiers require separate commercial review.

providers.integration_complexity: low for a synchronous adapter, but elevated operational risk from model lifecycle ambiguity and absent durable provider identity

findings.claim: Current multilingual models document Spanish support, including Spanish from Spain and Mexico for Multilingual v2; no Colombian locale-specific voice was documented.
The API supports streamed MP3, Opus, and raw 16-bit PCM at multiple sample rates; 44.1 kHz PCM is plan gated rather than universally available.
Text-to-speech with timestamps returns character-level alignment with the same streamed generation response.
The reviewed API is synchronous or streaming and does not document an asynchronous remote-job lifecycle or provider-side idempotency key.
Public API prices are character based, with Flash or Turbo cheaper than Multilingual v2 or v3; subscription plan and overage details remain relevant to total spend.
Default retention permits troubleshooting and service improvement; enterprise zero-retention mode removes most TTS text and audio after processing.
Paid-plan output may be used commercially, while the terms grant the provider a broad service and improvement license unless prospective data-use controls apply; legal review is required.
A public provider status page exists, but no contractual API SLA was verified in the reviewed official material.
The public voice catalog is extensive, but current default voices are scheduled to expire on 2026-12-31, so ORION cannot treat catalog voice identifiers as permanently stable.

Current Gemini TTS and Cloud TTS models support LINEAR16 or PCM plus compressed formats; model-specific encoding and sample-rate constraints require adapter validation.
The newest documented Gemini TTS families include preview model names and token-based billing, while established Cloud TTS families remain character priced.

findings.claim: Polly documents Mexican Spanish and United States Spanish voices, but no Colombian locale-specific voice.
Synchronous synthesis supports MP3, Ogg Vorbis, and raw 16-bit mono PCM; raw PCM is limited to 8 or 16 kHz, below ORION's current 24 kHz WAV baseline.
Asynchronous synthesis has a durable task identity and status but writes output to S3, introducing cloud storage and identity dependencies.
Speech marks provide sentence, word, viseme, and SSML timing, but are returned instead of audio and therefore require a separate priced synthesis request.
Public per-character prices are available for Standard, Neural, Generative, and Long-form engines.
Engine-specific throttling, concurrency, and duration limits are publicly documented, supporting bounded retries after clearly non-ambiguous failures.
AWS documents service-improvement use and cross-region storage unless an organization-level AI service opt-out policy is applied.
Commercial use remains governed by the AWS agreement and service terms; no Polly-specific output-ownership conclusion was established, so legal review remains required.
Amazon Polly is covered by the Amazon Machine Learning Language Service SLA, last updated in 2023.

recommendation.rationale: Azure is the strongest first listening-test candidate because it documents Colombian Spanish voices, production PCM, word boundaries, and a recovery-friendly batch identity. It is not selected because exact current pricing was not verified, legal review is incomplete, and no controlled listening evidence exists. Google is the secondary candidate because its pricing, privacy, SLA, and format evidence are strong, although it lacks a documented Colombian voice and long-audio mode requires cloud storage.

risks.description: Documentation cannot establish naturalness, pronunciation, or cross-segment consistency for ORION's Spanish narration.
Azure numeric pay-as-you-go pricing was not visible in the accessible official regional page, preventing a complete cost ceiling.
Provider terms, output rights, disclosure duties, and data-processing choices require product and legal approval before real narration is enabled.
Synchronous providers generally lack a durable remote identity, so ambiguous submission must remain uncertain and require deliberate recovery.
Google and AWS long-audio paths require provider cloud storage, which should not be introduced for the initial 30-second to 3-minute use case.
Voice cloning and custom voices add consent, identity, retention, and commercial complexity outside the initial release.
